problems: Claims that running the missing-pack listing without an active target set does not reveal these packs; comment 1 suggests exactly that command to list all missing packs.
cause_fixed: The mlops target line adds a target set outside the active target selection. csolution loads packs only for the selected contexts, and the missing-pack listing does not extend to target sets named under mlops, so a pack needed only by that set is not reported or installed until that target is selected.
fix_fixed: Workaround: declare the missing pack in the top-level solution file (the thread adds ARM::SSE_320_BSP@1.1.0 to sds.csolution.yml) so it is always loaded, or select the mlops target set so the pack is installed.

cause_fixed: Pre_Include_Global.h is a C/C++ pre-include that the build adds only to C/C++ compilation. Assembly files are not preprocessed with it; maintainers chose to handle C/C++ and assembly includes separately, so adding assembly support was declined.
fix_fixed: The thread gives no workaround for assembly macros. It only notes that the add-path-asm node was created to separate assembly include paths from add-path.

The cause names no second peripheral; the thread's message names 'POK' overlapping 'ASG' and the body describes the ASG module's two bus interfaces.
cause_fixed: The SVD describes one peripheral with a single address block whose size spans a large range that contains a second bus interface of the same module. Since the block is assumed to be one continuous range, its extent runs into the address range of another peripheral, which svdconv reports as an overlap.
fix_fixed: Split the module into two peripherals, ASG-low at 0x50097000 and ASG-high at 0x58010000, each with a compact 0x1000 address block covering its register range and sharing groupName ASG. This is the workaround suggested by a commenter; the thread does not confirm that it removes the warning.

cause_fixed: For SVD files from a local pack repository, the cbuild-run file stores a path relative to the current directory rather than an absolute path. A launcher such as JLINK_Server that resolves that path against its working directory can fail to find the file when the working directory changes. pyOCD already resolves relative paths against the cbuild-run file's own location, so only the other consumer is affected.
fix_fixed: No confirmed fix. Proposed: resolve SVD paths against the cbuild-run location where the J-Link server command line is built (for example around getSvdFilePaths in vscode-cmsis-debugger). A vscode-cmsis-debugger pull request (PR 815) is believed by one commenter to address this, but review was still pending. Absolute paths for local SVD files were proposed in the report but questioned by maintainers.

cause_fixed: The Notes column applies a different minimum-width behaviour to its header cell than to its data cells. When the column is shrunk, the data cells keep narrowing while the header stops, so their right edges no longer line up. The data rows also do not extend to the viewport edge when the combined column widths are smaller than the available space.
fix_fixed: The issue is closed and a comment states it was validated with CMSIS Debugger 1.9.1-9-gda28d9a, which the thread reports as behaving correctly. The thread does not describe the code change or any workaround.

The cause is stated as the debug agent's failure to advance the PC on resume; the thread only reports that the PC stays at the BKPT and that the behaviour is a pyOCD matter, so the mechanism is inferred rather than given.
cause_fixed: A BKPT instruction placed in the source halts the core when it is executed. On resume the program counter was not advanced past the instruction, so continuing halted again at the same address.
fix_fixed: pyOCD now steps over a BKPT instruction on both Step and Continue, matching the behaviour of uVision.

The thread says power-cycling restores debugging and the RESET button solves the problem, which is supported; the wording 'the reporter saw this mainly on slow machines' is a loose paraphrase of comment 5.
cause_fixed: The thread suggests a timing issue: the debug adapter's disconnect timeout may expire before pyOCD finishes its disconnect sequence, so pyOCD is forcefully terminated. The reporter found this reproducible on a slowed-down machine with a lowered timeout, and noted it may also involve genuine disconnect trouble with this board. The root cause is not confirmed.
fix_fixed: Workaround: raise serverDisconnectTimeout in the launch configuration (3000 ms in the example given). Pressing the board RESET button or power-cycling the board restores debugging. A higher timeout for managed launch configurations is tracked in #1293.

Fix says to use GDB 18.1 'or later'; the thread mentions only 18.1 and does not offer it as a workaround
Cause gives the affected GDB range as '14.2 through 17.2'; the thread lists only 14.2, 15.2, 16.3, 17.1 and 17.2
Cause states as fact that pyOCD cannot match the selector; the thread says this 'appears' to happen
Fix describes how PR #2052 maps the negative selector back to the positive ID; the thread only suggests this approach and does not show the PR's code
cause_fixed: With RTOS awareness enabled, thread IDs at or above 0x80000000 are valid positive 32-bit values. In the inspected source of GDB 14.2, 15.2, 16.3, 17.1 and 17.2, GDB sends such IDs to the GDB server as negative hexadecimal numbers, which appears to stop pyOCD from matching the selector to the thread, leaving execution stopped at the breakpoint.
fix_fixed: Use a pyOCD build that includes the fix from PR #2052. The reporter confirmed on an NXP IMXRT1050-EVK that execution resumes after a breakpoint in an RTOS thread with this fix. The thread does not name a pyOCD release that contains it.
versions_fixed: Affected GDB releases: 14.2, 15.2, 16.3, 17.1, 17.2. GDB 18.1 changes the encoding. The pyOCD release containing PR #2052 is not named in the thread.

Resolution 'workaround' is only partly supported. The PL10-CNANO workaround is already in the modified CMSIS Run task and the T2G-B-H behaviour is described, but the issue is open and no release fixes it.
cause_fixed: The debug sequences always halt the device after reset, so a plain pyocd run right after reset can stop at an unexpected address. The thread does not explain why the sysresetreq reset type avoids this; it only reports that it works on these boards.
fix_fixed: Workaround: run pyocd run with -O reset_type=sysresetreq for affected boards such as the Microchip PL10-CNANO (already in the modified CMSIS Run task) and the Infineon T2G-B-H. A complete fix needs the debug description spec update and pyOCD 1.10.0 support, then a DFP update; this is not yet released.
versions_fixed: pyOCD 1.10.0 (needed for the fix); the debug description spec change is required too. Not released at the time of the thread.

cause_fixed: The start processor (start-pname) was set automatically from the order of the cproject.yml entries, so the first one became the start processor. It was not selectable when the device was specified only in cproject.yml and not in the target-type.
fix_fixed: Workaround: add start-pname manually under the debugger node, or add a device entry under the target-type in the csolution file, which makes the start processor selectable. The maintainers later changed the extension to read device and processor names from the generated *.cbuild.yml files, so the start processor becomes selectable without editing the target-type.

cause_fixed: Per the reporter's analysis, when the FLM describes one sector range covering the whole flash region, pyOCD creates no subregions and does not copy FlashDevice.valEmpty to the parent region's erased_byte_value, which stays at the default 0xFF; the image builder then pads sparse HEX holes with 0xFF.
fix_fixed: Suggested fix: propagate FlashDevice.valEmpty to the parent flash region's erased_byte_value, including when no subregion is created. problems: Cause generalizes to 'some CMSIS-DAP v2 probes'; the thread only shows the Microchip PICkit Basic probe.
'The maintainers implemented this in PR #2061' overstates the thread: a PR is linked and the maintainer says it implements the workaround, but its merge status is not shown.
'Not yet released when the thread was read' is not stated in the thread; only the open PR is shown.
The probe-firmware fix is attributed to the maintainers as the 'root fix'; the thread only says the probe should not send the ZLP.
cause_fixed: A CMSIS-DAP v2 probe (Microchip PICkit Basic) ends an IN transfer with a zero-length packet when the reply is exactly the DAP packet size, here 512 bytes. pyOCD reads one USB packet per command, so the empty packet is taken as the reply to the next command. The real reply stays in the probe and every later command is out of step until the probe is replugged.
fix_fixed: Make the receive task in pyOCD's CMSIS-DAP v2 backend ignore zero-length reads and keep reading until it gets data, since no valid CMSIS-DAP reply is empty. PR #2061 implements this workaround; the thread does not show it merged or released. The probe firmware should stop sending the zero-length packet, which the maintainer says is the proper fix.
versions_fixed: pyOCD 0.45.1 with Microchip PICkit Basic CMSIS-DAP v2 firmware on Windows 10; workaround in PR #2061.
